A fresh disjoint panel bounds the objective margin without reusing a selection panel. result.hypothesis: Establish the initial baseline for the human-defined objective.
result.hypothesis_assessment: The automatic baseline carries no Researcher hypothesis, so this assesses the measurement-round questions that framed the evidence. The round-1 concern that the 14-20 cm training annulus would fail to generalize to the full 6-20 cm official distribution is weakened: the 6-10 and 10-14 cm bands succeed at ~97.6%, no worse than the trained 14-20 cm bands. The round-1/round-2 expectation that checkpoint-100352 is the strongest available policy on the full distribution is supported: it leads both disjoint 1000-episode panels and every paired comparison. The round-3 expectation that the unmeasured plateau checkpoints checkpoint-115712 or checkpoint-105472 would reduce the shared negative-angle residual is contradicted: both score 96.7% on the same panel, below checkpoint-100352, and exhibit the same negative-angle deficit. Overall the investigation outcome is partially supported to inconclusive at the objective level: the baseline is the best measured policy so far, but it remains ~0.7 points below the 98% objective and the originally hypothesized near-target generalization gap is not the binding deficit. Limits: the full-range estimates derive from panels that also ranked checkpoints, and the task-reference result is selection-contaminated; the angular attribution is descriptive.

requested_evaluations.label: full-distribution evaluation of peak-proxy checkpoint
requested_evaluations.selection: Highest training-success proxy of all 24 candidates (0.97), so it is the most plausible working policy, but its proxy was measured only on 14-20 cm; measuring it on the full 6-20 cm panel tests whether that peak survives the untrained near-target region.

requested_evaluations.label: full-distribution evaluation of final checkpoint
requested_evaluations.selection: Final checkpoint (120,832 steps, proxy 0.95) with the most accumulated training; measuring it on the same panel as checkpoint-100352 decides whether the final update improved or degraded full-distribution behavior, which determines whether later checkpoints should parent the next experiment.

requested_evaluations.label: full-distribution evaluation of plateau-onset checkpoint
requested_evaluations.selection: First checkpoint in the high-proxy plateau (0.93) after the steep climb from 0.71 at step 90112, so it marks where the policy changed behavior; measuring it on the same panel tests whether the plateau is stable across steps and whether an earlier checkpoint generalizes better than the later ones.

requested_evaluations.label: disjoint-panel reproduction of leading candidate
requested_evaluations.selection: checkpoint-100352 scored 99.5% (199/200) on the selection panel, the highest of the three measured checkpoints, but that panel ranked the models and its 1-episode edge over checkpoint-120832 and checkpoint-95232 is within noise; its only failure was the persistent far-target reach failure at episode seed 5099 (r=16.37 cm). Measuring it on a 1000-episode panel disjoint from 5000-5199 gives an independent estimate of its true full-range success and of the frequency of hard targets like seed 5099, which decides whether the campaign requests the terminal benchmark now or closes and trains a further experiment.

requested_evaluations.label: disjoint-panel evaluation of final checkpoint
requested_evaluations.selection: checkpoint-120832 is the final checkpoint (120,832 steps, most accumulated training) and tied checkpoint-95232 at 99.0% while losing to checkpoint-100352 by one episode on the panel that selected the working candidate; its unique failure was a hold-boundary oscillation (episode seed 5013, max consecutive hold 5 of 100, 244 hold interruptions), a different mode from checkpoint-100352's reach failure. Measuring it on the same disjoint 1000-episode panel decides which checkpoint becomes the working and best-known policy on evidence independent of the selection panel.

task_reference_evaluations.selection: checkpoint-100352 has never been measured on the human-owned task-reference evaluator, which executes the protected original task with code independent of robot_learning/scenario/evaluation.py. working_lineage.reason: checkpoint-100352 is the strongest measured policy of experiment 1: 97.3% and 97.2% on two disjoint 1000-episode full-range panels, 99.5% on the 200-episode selection panel and 98.0% on the task-reference panel, and it wins every paired comparison (12 vs 1 over 1200 episodes against checkpoint-120832, 7 vs 1 against checkpoint-115712, 6 vs 0 against checkpoint-105472). Its residual failures are localized to the -120 to -160 degree target sector inside the trained radius range, so it is both the best available baseline and the most informative parent for the next experiment.
